name: AZ-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 13 points and Grijalva is the incumbent
Grijalva holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 99%
No public polls or expert ratings; outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's 13-point Democratic lean, Grijalva's incumbency, and her roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge over Butierez point to a comfortable win, and prediction markets price her near certain. With no polls available, the margin rests on fundamentals and carries wider-than-usual uncertainty.
model.watch: Any polling of the race showing a far narrower margin, or a sharply favorable Republican national environment, would be the main reason to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arizona's 7th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of about 13 points toward Democrats. Adelita Grijalva holds the seat as the incumbent and is running for a full term. She has raised roughly $2.3 million, about ten times the $224,000 collected by Republican Daniel Butierez, who had only about $11,000 on hand. Outside groups have spent modestly to support her and little to oppose her.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at about 99%. The expected margin is roughly 22 points, with meaningful uncertainty because direct polling evidence is absent. The seat remains in the Safe Democratic column.
